title: QUIC RFC 9221 DATAGRAM Architecture
purpose: Define the implementation boundary for RFC 9221 DATAGRAM support, including transport-parameter state, DATAGRAM frame codec behavior, receive-side runtime integration, and core runtime send integration.
design_summary: The first implementation slices add the RFC 9221 wire, negotiation, receive, and core send foundation. `QuicTransportParameters` carries `MaxDatagramFrameSize`, the transport-parameter codec parses and formats parameter `0x20`, 0-RTT remembered transport-parameter state can preserve and validate the DATAGRAM size limit, and `QuicFrameCodec` parses and formats DATAGRAM frame types `0x30` and `0x31`. The application packet ingress path delivers valid protected 1-RTT DATAGRAM frames through a distinct `QuicConnectionDeliverDatagramEffect`, rejects unadvertised or oversized DATAGRAM frames, and treats DATAGRAM as forbidden in weakly protected packet contexts. The outbound path exposes `QuicConnection.SendDatagramAsync`, builds length-carrying DATAGRAM frames, rejects missing peer support and oversized frames, accounts protected packets through congestion state, drops congestion-blocked DATAGRAM sends without a transport error, and tracks sent DATAGRAM packets as ack-eliciting but non-retransmittable with no stream association. HTTP Datagrams adapter behavior and application ACK/loss notification APIs remain explicit follow-up work.
data_and_state_considerations: The `MaxDatagramFrameSize` value is stored as a nullable transport-parameter field so absence remains distinguishable from an advertised zero value while the effective unsupported default remains zero. `QuicDatagramFrame` owns a copied payload byte array to keep parser output independent of attacker-controlled input buffers. `QuicConnectionDeliverDatagramEffect` is the receive-side application DATAGRAM signal. The existing `QuicConnectionSendDatagramEffect` remains UDP-packet emission and is not reused as an RFC 9221 application DATAGRAM signal.
edge_cases_and_constraints: DATAGRAM frame type `0x30` consumes the rest of the packet payload and is only safe as the final frame in a QUIC packet.
DATAGRAM frame type `0x31` carries an explicit varint Length field and can be parsed before later coalesced frames.
Receive-side runtime handling rejects local unsupported DATAGRAM use before delivery.
Outbound runtime send handling rejects peer unsupported DATAGRAM use before packet assembly.
Outbound DATAGRAM frames use type `0x31` so padding or future coalesced frames cannot be mistaken for DATAGRAM payload bytes.
Congestion-blocked outbound DATAGRAM sends are dropped by this slice instead of queued.
0-RTT DATAGRAM sending remains blocked until the application profile and early-data gate are explicitly implemented.
risks: The core runtime send floor can be mistaken for HTTP Datagrams, CONNECT-UDP, or MASQUE support, which remains out of scope.
The existing runtime effect name `QuicConnectionSendDatagramEffect` can confuse UDP datagram emission with RFC 9221 application DATAGRAM frames.
Transport-parameter 0-RTT memory is implemented, but actual 0-RTT DATAGRAM transmission remains out of scope for this slice.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This artifact currently covers canonical requirements plus transport-parameter, frame-codec, receive-side 1-RTT DATAGRAM handling, and core runtime send support for peer-gated application DATAGRAM payloads. HTTP Datagrams adapter behavior, optional ACK/loss application notifications, 0-RTT DATAGRAM transmission, benchmarks, and higher-level adapter policy remain follow-up work.
